correctness.rationale: Direct linearization at a=g(E)>0 gives v_t=-a(v_x+kappa v), since u_E'+kappa u_E=0, with v(t,0)=b m(t), b=-Bg'(E)/a^2 and m=integral v. Scaling time by a gives after transit the stated truncated exponential renewal equation and 1-R(1-e^-k)=h'(E)/a. For R<=0 the shifted characteristic equation cannot have a root with Re s>=0 by the modulus bound. For subcritical R>0 the integral modulus is bounded by R(1-e^-k)<1; for supercritical R>0 the real integral decreases strictly to zero and yields a positive root. At equality the unmultiplied characteristic function has nonzero derivative at zero. At s=i omega the real and imaginary equations, for R>0, force (k omega)(e^k-cos(k omega))=k sin(k omega), impossible for omega nonzero since e^k-1>k. The root s=-1 introduced by clearing the denominator is not used. On L1 the transport semigroup is eventually compact: after one transit v(sigma,x)=b e^(-kappa x)m(sigma-x), and differentiation of the integral in moving-endpoint coordinates gives m'=(b-kappa)m-b e^(-kappa L)m(sigma-L). Finite-time mass bounds from the characteristic Volterra equation give equi-Lipschitz profiles after two transits. Thus exclusion of closed-right-half-plane roots gives exponential decay of the full linearized evolution, not only of a formal mode. The example independently follows from h(3/5+x)=21/125+x^3-2x/25, with extrema x=±sqrt(6)/15 and central roots x=0,±sqrt(2)/5. The equal-slope case is neutral in the spectral sense stated, not positive-real instability; no nonlinear basin follows. Frozen verify.py was inspected, not executed.

value.rationale: The result converts a stationary fold diagnostic into a complete linear criterion for a natural, finite-residence subclass. In particular the imaginary-root exclusion for any real feedback is useful beyond calculating three stationary roots and prevents mistaking the distributed memory in this subclass for a mechanism of oscillatory linear destabilization. The classified example illustrates the distinction; it does not claim nonlinear hysteresis dynamics or basins.
